title: WeHOPE’s building: the deeds from the insider-linked company
question: What does the county record show about the building WeHOPE bought from a company tied to one of its officers?
finding: San Mateo County's index shows 3 deeds from Action Associates Inc to WeHOPE in East Palo Alto: one on 28 September 2018 (transfer tax $1,760) and two on 18 October 2024 (transfer tax $4,950 on one, $0 on the other). WeHOPE's land and buildings on its own returns went from $1,812,293 at the end of 2023 to $6,781,102 at the end of 2024, up $4,968,809; the 2024 return reports the $4,555,548 building transaction. The transfer tax comes to $1.00 per $1,000 of that rise, and the 2018 tax to $0.97 per $1,000 of the 2020 book value: the two purchases are in proportion. The same index lists 3 notices of State tax lien against the name WEHOPE (2012, and twice in 2021), each later released; found by a name search, the records do not show whether they concern this organization or another party of the same name.
how: Index rows saved from the county's free RecorderWorks search for the names WEHOPE and ACTION ASSOCIATES; grantor, grantee and transfer tax are shown only for deeds whose detail page was opened. Land and buildings are the cost columns of Form 990 Schedule D (Part VI) on WeHOPE's 2020-2024 returns. The ratio is the transfer tax divided by the change in book value, per $1,000.
limits: The index gives the tax, not the price, and the book value includes improvements and costs that are not the price. The 2018 purchase from the same company predates the returns on disk, so whether it was reported as an insider transaction cannot be checked here. The tax liens are a name match on WEHOPE in the county index; the index does not say what tax was owed, and all were released. Buying from a related company is permitted when the price is fair and independent directors approve it.
